query: For bulk HfNbTaTiZr, what testable hypothesis could an unspecified predictive approach make to overcome the limited accuracy of available analytical predictions and their usual restriction to perfect, defect-free crystals? Address the nearly 0–200 K regime and the 300–1200 K regime, for which measurements also exist on a specimen containing 1 wt.% oxygen; explain why the approach should improve accuracy, predict its advantage over existing analytical approaches, define its temperature and sample applicability limits, identify supporting prior evidence, and specify a held-out conductivity benchmark and result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: A combined electronic transport simulation approach that integrates CPA for quantum averaging of disorder with actively learned MTPs for local atomic relaxations will accurately predict the electronic conductivity of bulk HfNbTaTiZr with ~1 wt% oxygen impurities over both the 0–200 K and 300–1200 K regimes, outperforming conventional analytical predictions based on perfect, defect‐free crystals.
generation.material_initial_state: Bulk HfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy containing approximately 1 wt% oxygen impurities.
generation.intervention: Apply a coupled CPA/MTP computational framework that incorporates scattering effects from disordered lattice sites and local relaxation due to oxygen defects.
generation.conditions: Measurements and simulations will be compared over two temperature regimes: a low-temperature regime (0–200 K) and a high-temperature regime (300–1200 K) under ambient pressure conditions.
generation.structural_mediator: The oxygen impurity induces local lattice distortions and defect states which are explicitly modeled by the MTP, while CPA accounts for the average effects of chemical and topological disorder.
generation.mechanism: CPA precisely captures abrupt changes in the Fermi-surface topology and electron scattering from the disordered alloy matrix, and the actively learned MTP accurately simulates local relaxation around oxygen defects. Together, these resolve the limitations of analytical models that assume defect-free crystals.
generation.predicted_outcome: The combined CPA/MTP approach is expected to predict electronic transport properties (e.g., electrical conductivity/resistivity) with a relative error of less than ~10% compared to experimental measurements in both temperature regimes, substantially improving upon the >20% error typically observed with traditional perfect-crystal models.
generation.baseline: Analytical predictions based on ideal, defect-free crystal models which neglect local lattice relaxations and scattering from oxygen-induced defects.
generation.boundary: The predictive improvement is anticipated to hold specifically for bulk HfNbTaTiZr alloys containing up to ~1 wt% oxygen; predictions outside the 0–200 K and 300–1200 K temperature regimes or for significantly higher impurity levels may not be reliable.
generation.uncertainty: There is uncertainty regarding the model’s accuracy at ultra-low temperatures (<5 K) where quantum coherence effects may become significant, and the quantitative error margins might vary with slight differences in oxygen content or microstructural inhomogeneities.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare bulk HfNbTaTiZr samples with a controlled ~1 wt% oxygen content. Measure the temperature-dependent electrical conductivity (or resistivity) using a cryogenic setup for the 0–200 K regime and a high-temperature furnace with controlled atmosphere for the 300–1200 K regime. Simultaneously perform the combined CPA/MTP simulations under the same compositional and temperature conditions.
measurements: Electrical conductivity/resistivity as a function of temperature across the two regimes.
Microstructural/defect characterization confirming oxygen distribution and lattice distortions.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the experimentally measured conductivity/resistivity deviates by more than ~15% from the predicted values in either the low-temperature or high-temperature regime, or if the improvement over conventional analytical predictions is not statistically significant, then the hypothesis that the CPA/MTP approach offers superior predictive accuracy will be falsified.

cited_evidence.text: The crucial point of our approach is to enhance the simulation efficiency by employing the most suitable method for different sets of properties. Specifically, CPA’s quantum mechanical treatment of solid solutions and its analytical nature eliminates finite-size cell effects and sampling errors related to random atomic configurations, making it excel in calculations of the concentration dependence of properties that are relatively insensitive to local relaxations, such as elastic constants and misfit volumes. In comparison to supercell calculations with MLIPs, CPA is especially superior in accuracy when dealing with abrupt changes of the Fermi-surface topology, which is often encountered in bcc alloys and can have a significant impact on the concentration dependence of properties. On the other hand, ab initio based MTP methodology surpasses CPA in dealing with defects and special geometries, such as surfaces, due to its capability to incorporate local atomic relaxations.

cited_evidence.text: The negative-sloping σε within the Fermi-level region and the assumption of negatively charged carriers, e=-e (electrons) reproduce quantitatively the NTC electrical resistivity and the positive thermopower with all their nonlinear features in the entire measured temperature range 2–400 K for both samples. Knowing σT and ST, the electronic thermal conductivity κelT was calculated from Eqs. (4a,b) and is presented by solid lines in Fig. 3c. It is observed that the calculated κelHEAT and κelMGT account for the majority part of the experimental total thermal conductivities κHEAT and κMGT, supporting the assumption that the phononic thermal conductivity κph is small for both samples. The negative derivative dσ/dε<0 and the associated dg/dε<0 within the Fermi-level region also consistently explain the positive sign of the Hall coefficient RH and hence support the relation RH∝-dg/dεεF for the investigated chemically and topologically disordered HEA and MG samples.

chosen.approach: Electronic transport modeling in disordered alloys via CPA/MTP
